doc: Chapter 5, DART (September 2022) (issue #49; story: docs/design/story-v0.3.0.md). Every fact from NASA pages (S-dart-nasa, S-dart-nasa-period, S-dart-nssdc). The crew fly it from mission control; this time they crash with confidence (the story's line). Same format as lcross.json.
mission: Between intro and outro the player plays the mission: find Dimorphos, steer, the last picture, the measurement weeks later (scripts/screens/dart.gd).

intro.title: Mission 5: DART
intro.sub: September 26, 2022 · Dimorphos, 11 million km from Earth

intro.text: Thirteen years after the Moon, a new plan: push an asteroid, and see if it moves.
intro.fact: DART launched on November 24, 2021, on a Falcon 9 from Vandenberg, in California.

intro.text: It is a test. We hit the small moon of an asteroid and see if its orbit changes.
intro.fact: Dimorphos, 160 meters across, orbits Didymos, 780 meters across.

intro.text: We have crashed into the Moon already. This time we crash with confidence.
Its orbit takes 11 hours and 55 minutes. After us, it should take less.
intro.fact: Before DART's impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit Didymos.

intro.text: And I aim at the little one. Not the big one. The little one.
Two weeks before, a tiny Italian satellite let go of DART, to follow it and watch.
intro.fact: LICIACube, from the Italian Space Agency, was released on September 11 and followed about 3 minutes behind DART.

intro.text: Four hours out. The camera is on. Find the little moon.
intro.fact: In the last 4 hours, DART's camera, DRACO, and its autonomous navigation, SMARTNav, found and targeted the asteroid.

outro.text: 23:14 UT, as Earth heard it. DART is gone. Three minutes later, LICIACube flies past the cloud of rock it threw out.
outro.fact: The impact was received on Earth at 23:14 UT; LICIACube flew by about 3 minutes after, imaging the plume.

outro.text: Thirty-two minutes! Its orbit is thirty-two minutes shorter!
outro.fact: NASA confirmed the impact shortened Dimorphos's orbit to 11 hours 23 minutes: 32 minutes, plus or minus about 2.

outro.text: They hoped for seventy-three seconds. We gave them thirty-two minutes.
outro.fact: NASA had set a change of 73 seconds or more as the minimum for success.

outro.text: I told you. The little one.
One mission left. The biggest one. And this time, somebody sits in the seat.
